deep.reconstruction:
Context. Cote 154 is Grothendieck's 1983-84 file on 'systèmes de pseudo-droites', that is, arrangements of pseudolines in the real projective plane (equivalently, families of curves in a Möbius band). The sheet is recycled fan-fold computer paper: a JES2 job banner 'GUTS', dated 16 Aug 82. The printed text has nothing to do with the mathematics. All mathematical content is in the coloured hand drawings, with only scattered letter labels. No sentences or statements appear.

(1) Top-left and top-centre: 'stars' (étoiles), several pseudolines passing through one multiple point.
- Short transverse orange ticks and hatching on one side of each strand mark sides or local orientations.
- Shaded triangles and blue- or green-marked ends near the extremities mark the ends of the strands.
- On the next page these are called 'bouts (bleus) marqués' (marked blue ends).
- So these are local models of a multiple point, with markings recording how the ends are attached at infinity or to a boundary.

(2) Top-right: two green lines crossing twice. This is a digon, which cannot occur for two pseudolines in RP^2: they meet exactly once. It is presumably drawn as the forbidden or degenerate configuration, or as the lift of a single crossing in a double cover or affine picture. The isolated small green cross is the elementary single crossing.

(3) Bottom-left: two 'figure-eight' or circle figures. Each is a closed green band (a 'canal', channel) with two orange strands D, D' running through it. The strands enter and leave at points x, y and x', y'.
- In the first figure two discs are joined along a short neck, where the labels D, D' are repeated. This matches the crossed-out 'canaux des huit' on the next page.
- The small square figure (labels x0, x, y, y0 / x', y', y'0) is a local cut-and-paste picture. Two strands crossing inside a rectangular piece of channel are cut along the top and bottom segments [x0, y0] and [x', y'], then reglued.

(4) Bottom-centre: a cell complex with hatched green regions (faces, or channel regions) and orange crossings. Labels a, b sit on dashed arcs around crossings; x, y, x0, y0, u, u0 sit at the attaching points. It appears to describe how several channels meet at crossings, i.e. a decomposition of the arrangement into channels joined at stars.

(5) Bottom-right: two 'bump' diagrams. A green base curve runs x, x0, y0, y in the first and u, u0, v0, v in the second. It passes just below a crossing of two orange strands; the subarc [x0, y0] (resp. [u0, v0]) is marked. A brown curve a (resp. b) goes over the crossing and returns to the base line.
- This is the standard picture of pushing a pseudoline across a crossing: the triangle flip or mutation, the Reidemeister-III-type move.
- Equivalently, it compares two isotopic positions of a curve relative to a vertex.

Overall reading. Grothendieck is developing a combinatorial-topological description of pseudoline arrangements. He decomposes them into 'canaux' (channels between marked ends) and isolated exceptional 'étoiles' (multiple points), and considers the local moves that sweep a curve over a crossing. The next page confirms this: 'canaux : lieu des cours entre bouts (bleus) marqués, et étoiles exceptionnelles isolées (ou sous-étoiles)'. The previous page assigns signs (+/-) to crossings of oriented curves.
errors: The two green lines crossing twice (top right) cannot represent two pseudolines in RP^2, which meet exactly once. Presumably this is intentional (forbidden configuration or a covering/affine picture), but the page gives no explanation.
Labels are sparse and partly illegible. The precise roles of a, b and of the subscripted points cannot be fixed from this page alone, so the reconstruction is interpretive.

ideas.what: Multiple points ('étoiles') of a pseudoline arrangement with marked ends/sides
ideas.modern_name: non-simple arrangement; local sequence of a vertex; wiring-diagram ends
ideas.where_published: Grothendieck's pseudoline work is not published; only archive notes (cotes 150s) exist.

ideas.what: Sweeping a pseudoline across a crossing (bump diagrams with curves a, b over a vertex)
ideas.modern_name: triangle flip / mutation; Ringel's theorem on flip-connectivity of simple arrangements
ideas.usually_credited_to: G. Ringel (1956); later Goodman–Pollack, Björner–Las Vergnas–Sturmfels–White–Ziegler (Oriented Matroids)

ideas.what: Decomposition of an arrangement into 'channels' between marked ends plus isolated exceptional stars; cut-and-paste along channel segments
ideas.modern_name: closest: cell decompositions / wiring diagrams, zones of an arrangement
ideas.usually_credited_to: zones: Goodman–Pollack, zone theorem (Chazelle–Guibas–Lee, Edelsbrunner et al.); wiring diagrams: Goodman (1980)

ideas.what: Signs/orientations at crossings (previous page) combined with these local pictures

missed.claim: Grothendieck sketches a structure theory of pseudoline arrangements organised around 'canaux' (channels joining marked ends, including figure-eight channels) and isolated exceptional stars. This is a viewpoint not obviously identical to zones or wiring diagrams. It is left as drawings without a stated theorem.
missed.quote: canaux : lieu des cours entre bouts (bleus) marqués, et étoiles exceptionnelles isolées (ou sous-étoiles) [next page]; labels D, D', x', y' on the 'huit' figures
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Mildly relevant to the history of Grothendieck's late interest in combinatorial topology of RP^2. Any mathematical novelty would require reconstructing the full file; this page alone shows only standard local moves.

deep.surprise_reason: The page has wordless sketches of standard local configurations in pseudoline arrangements: multiple points, crossings, triangle-flip bump pictures and a channel cut-and-paste. These are known since Ringel and Goodman–Pollack. Only the 'canaux' organisation is idiosyncratic, and it is not developed here.
transcription_corrections: The printed banner is recycled listing paper ('//* GUTS 0108 I', JES2 STC 108, 16 AUG 82) and is unrelated to the mathematics.
Square figure labels: top row x0, x, y, y0; bottom row x'0, x', y', y'0 (rather than 'x'' y'0' / 'x'' y''').
Right bump figures: first has curve a over a crossing with base points x, x0, y0, y; second has curve b with base points u, u0, v0, v ('v0', not 'u0', for the second inner point).
Top-right shows two green lines crossing twice (a digon), and a separate single green cross appears in the middle-left among the banner lines.
